_comment: ORGANISER ONLY - never served to participants. Canonical navigation path through the verified paper-to-paper graph.

transitions.narrative: Ratnasamy & McCanne infer a multicast tree from what receivers observe. Ni & Tatikonda cite them among multicast-probing approaches to the same routing-topology inference problem and recast it with additive metrics, stating that it 'is similar to the phylogenetic inference problem in evolutionary biology' (p.5).

Bhamidi, Rajagopal & Roch (applied probability) discuss Ni & Tatikonda's neighbor-joining approach and state that both use distance-based phylogenetic techniques on additive tree metrics (p.5). They also explain why NJ itself is sample-hungry (p.7).

Bhamidi et al. cite Saitou & Nei (ref. [24]) and argue that multicast inference is 'in essence a special case of the standard model of DNA evolution', i.e. the phylogenetic tree reconstruction problem that neighbor-joining solves.

why_this_path: Every transition is backed by both a bibliographic fact (CITES) and a located methodological / conceptual / interpretive passage. The path also crosses three discipline groups (networking -> applied probability -> evolutionary biology), so a team has to read across vocabularies. It is not the shortest route; see alternative_paths.json.
